provisional: not in the GDD yet; spike value (spike B): lowest generated gauge baseline.

provisional: not in the GDD yet; spike value (spike B): corruption starts low.
Most a region gains a day from all its neighbours together. With the threat rise and the 5% pull, a region at the highest baseline settles under the overrun line even with every neighbour burning.
Unrest a day in a region while its raid line holds.
Chance each world day that something comes out of the wild into one region.
Smallest surge.
Largest surge.
Share of a surge each neighbouring region also takes.
Threat a day in a region whose starting settlement keeps a watch; nobody has to play for it.

Threat a day in an overrun region: what overran it spends itself and moves on, so an overrun is an episode, not an ending. MM1 World run: 30, not GDD 4.3's 25, so a run of surges on a small horizon ends with no more than 3 regions overrun.
A season (GDD 2.2).
At most one live system per this many regions inside the horizon.
Each world day, each spine cell inside the horizon rolls once for a new system.
A new system's least strength.
A new system's greatest strength.
No system grows stronger.
Footprint radius is 1 tile plus strength over this.
A system moves a tile every (this − strength ÷ weather-pace-per) ticks.
Under this strength a system loses a world day of life.
Steps of heading a system may turn toward the wind each world day.
The forecast is exact this far ahead.
Tiles at or under this elevation are low: dead zones pool there.
The horizon holds discovered regions and those within this many regions of one (GDD 4.2).
Share of surges that come from a dormant region just past the horizon, spilling into its awake neighbours.
Scarcity a region gains per unit gathered in it.
A system whose centre strays this far from every awake region's centre leaves the map.
Tiles at or over this elevation are high ground: clear weather lengthens sight there.
The ledger report's clock (GDD 4.7).
A structure's condition when built (GDD 4.16).
A starting settlement's defence: its watch, paid by its treasury (MM1 World run: at a holding's 60, one surge onto a settlement could raid it down in 3 days).
Defence a starting settlement's watch restores each world day, up to settlement-defence.
